assumptions_resolved: Live read-only verification, not the test suite, is what found both defects in this step. 980 tests passed over code that could not read the live lanes at all, because both failures need a real record written before the current conventions existed. That is the reason the plan requires a live gate as well as suites, and it is now the reason two new tests exist.

The exit-code change is a narrowing, not a relaxation. Exit 2 on --abandonment-audit is a factual claim that an expired author lane was found. A refusal never established that, so reporting it as 2 was a false positive with an operator cost: the scheduled run on 2026-09-16 at main head 3fdd16ef logged 'REFUSED: claim title must identify exactly one work issue for capacity transition events' and then '##[error]Expired author lane(s) detected', which is a report about lanes the instrument never read. Exit 3 already means unverifiable on this command and already outranks expiry. Every other command keeps the generic handler and keeps exiting 2, which the new test asserts directly.

Isolating the claim-identity read does not hide the unreadable claim. The row carries the claim number in both the capacity and the preview error, so the operator is told which claim to fix, and preview_edge_satisfied is forced false so an unreadable claim can never be counted as ready.

scripts/manage-migration-author-lanes.mjs is the repository's single protected coordination source. The nine open pull requests were checked against the rule in scripts/check-pr-source-collisions.mjs before it was edited and none of them touches that file, so there was no colliding pull request to wait behind. The rule was not bypassed.

Live proof at this head, all read-only: --abandonment-audit reports status UNVERIFIABLE with mutating false, zero actions carrying mutates true, all eight lanes described, capacity 8 issues / 7 actions / 1 unverifiable, six expired-unconfirmed-report actions, exit 3. That agrees with --queue-audit, which reports the same seven lanes without a live lease and one active lane. No database, preview, production or infrastructure write occurred, and no ref, branch or worktree was deleted.

The lifecycle was deliberately NOT applied to any live expired claim to demonstrate it. Six live lanes are reported as expired-unconfirmed; acting on any of them needs that claim's own current evidence and an authorised operator decision, and this plan is not that authority.
